The grey regions of the micrographs depict the solid content after sintering, and the dark regions depict the pores that are formed from ice crystals during processing. Through an innovation in the casting process, our approach in this research project was to introduce lateral pore gradients as depicted in Figure 3. The technology allows for continuous modification of solids loading during the development of pore formation as ice crystals grow through the cast slurry layer, yielding the capability to laterally grade pores for improved CO distribution over the nanoparticle catalyst. 2 13 Figure 3. Lateral pore grading provides uniform delivery of CO to the active catalyst as the concentration of 2 CO2 diminishes across scaled membranes. While the concept of changing solids loading during the casting process appears to be simple in design, the merit of this conceptualization has never been achieved. Further, in traditional tape casting, higher viscosity slurries make homogenization of the different solids loadings more challenging, further highlighting the value of the ice templating process with lower solids loading and, hence, lower viscosity slurry formulation. Combined with the recognized need for graded cross-sections to enhance CO delivery 2 (Weng, L .C. et al., 2018) and contact with an aqueous solution (Figure 4), the MSU innovation is designed to provide gradients in two discrete axes, providing new degrees of freedom for engineering catalyst and catalyst support membranes. 14 Figure 4.
